plan.title: AD lesional vs control skin: pre-DE sample QC
plan.analytical_narrative:
The question is purely diagnostic: before any differential-expression test on the 6 atopic-dermatitis lesional vs 6 control skin samples, characterise the twelve libraries and reach a keep/drop verdict on sample_01, which the data profile flags as having a library size roughly 4x below the median. The input is a 12000 x 13 gene-level count matrix from Salmon (counts.csv, first column gene ID + 12 sample columns) and a 12 x 2 sample table (metadata.csv: sample, condition), unpaired, single batch.

The work splits into three steps. T1S1 establishes the count-level facts that everything else rests on: per-sample library size, detected-gene counts, size factors, and how much of each library sits in the top few genes — the last is what distinguishes a merely shallow library from one dominated by a handful of transcripts. It also confirms the sample/column correspondence between the two files, since a silent mismatch would invalidate every downstream conclusion. T1S2 does the multivariate view on variance-stabilised data (VST via DESeq2, which handles the depth heterogeneity better than a plain log-CPM when one library is 4x down): PCA with condition and depth annotated, plus the sample-to-sample Euclidean distance matrix as a clustered heatmap. Because PCA on a 12-sample matrix with one shallow library can be driven by depth alone, this step explicitly tests the correlation of PC1/PC2 with log library size and repeats the embedding with sample_01 removed, so we can tell whether sample_01's position is a depth artefact or a genuine biological outlier. T1S3 turns those numbers into a defensible verdict: a small set of pre-declared criteria (depth relative to median, detection rate, PC association with depth, distance-based outlier rank, and whether excluding it changes the group separation) evaluated against the actual measurements, with an explicit power note — dropping sample_01 leaves 5 vs 6 and thins an already small design.

No differential testing is planned here; the user asked what the samples look like, not what differs. The two shallow-depth caveats that matter downstream — whether the Salmon counts carry a length correction and whether depth confounds condition — are recorded by T1S1 and T1S2 respectively so the eventual DE step inherits them rather than rediscovering them. No external reference data is needed; the analysis is self-contained on the two input CSVs.

A second PCA computed after removing sample_01, with a stated comparison of condition separation before and after.
caveats: With 12 samples, PCA is unstable; treat apparent clusters as descriptive, not as evidence of group structure.
VST behaves poorly when one library is extremely shallow — inspect the mean-variance trend and say so if the transformation looks strained.
Hierarchical clustering appearance depends on the linkage; state the linkage used and do not over-read a single dendrogram.

steps.name: Verdict on sample_01
steps.question: Should sample_01 be retained, retained with caution, or excluded from the atopic dermatitis lesional vs control differential-expression analysis, and what does either choice cost?
steps.description: Combine the metrics table from T1S1 and the PCA/distance results from T1S2 into an explicit, pre-declared decision rubric applied to sample_01 and, for fairness, to every other sample. Evaluate five criteria and record the measured value and a pass/borderline/fail call for each: (1) library size relative to the cohort median and in absolute counts; (2) detected genes at count >= 10, relative to the cohort; (3) library fraction in the top 50 genes relative to the cohort, as a check for a low-complexity library; (4) whether the sample is a distance-matrix outlier beyond the cohort distribution of mean sample-to-sample distances; (5) whether the sample's PCA position tracks depth (from the PC-versus-depth correlations) rather than condition, and whether removing it changed the condition separation. Then state a single verdict with reasoning, and state the cost of exclusion explicitly: which group sample_01 belongs to per metadata.csv, the resulting group sizes, and a plain statement that removing it leaves an unpaired design with one group at n=5 and materially reduced power. Recommend the concrete downstream handling that follows from the verdict — retain unmodified, retain but confirm the DE result is stable to its removal as a sensitivity analysis, or exclude — and note that if depth is confounded with condition group, that confound persists regardless of the decision. Write a short markdown QC report assembling the metrics table, the figures produced upstream, and the verdict.
steps.context: This is the deliverable the user asked for: a verdict on the sample that looks shallow, grounded in the numbers from T1S1 and T1S2 rather than in the profile's flag alone. Low depth on its own is a reason for caution, not automatic exclusion — a shallow library with normal complexity and a normal distance profile is usually usable, whereas one that is also low-complexity and a distance outlier is not.
constraints: State the decision criteria and their thresholds before reporting the outcome, and apply them to all 12 samples, not only sample_01.
Base every call on a value measured in T1S1 or T1S2; do not introduce new claims about the data.
State sample_01's condition group from metadata.csv and the exact group sizes that would result from exclusion.
Give one unambiguous verdict — retain, retain with sensitivity check, or exclude — not a list of options without a recommendation.
Do not run any differential-expression test in this step.
acceptance_criteria: A criteria table with the measured value and pass/borderline/fail call for all 12 samples across the five criteria.
A single stated verdict for sample_01 with the reasoning tied to specific measured values.
Explicit statement of post-exclusion group sizes and the power consequence of dropping to n=5 in one group.
A markdown QC report file assembling metrics, figures, and verdict.
An explicit note on whether library depth is associated with condition group across the cohort.
caveats: Shallow depth alone does not justify exclusion; avoid recommending removal on the depth flag without corroborating evidence from complexity or distance.
With n=6 per group, dropping a sample is expensive — say so rather than treating exclusion as free.
A verdict of 'retain with sensitivity check' is a legitimate outcome and should be given when the evidence is genuinely mixed.
